title: Face Sculpt #054 (한국 · 20대 · 광기 어린 · 도 아이 +1 · 성형 코 1단 · 하트형 턱 · 정면 · 메이크업 없음 · P200 · 혼합 금속 추 9개/귀 2구멍 · 배경 실외 비 오는 밤 청록·남색 네온 · 테마 펑크(안전핀·가시 스터드) · 스티커 · 렌즈 오드아이 앰버(하트 동공)|크림슨 레드(큰 동공))
prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, close-up beauty portrait. ONE woman, facing the camera straight on in a perfectly frontal portrait, her head level, both ears clearly visible on either side of her face, framed tightly from the very top of her head down to the line of her shoulders, the frame cutting off just below them, so the weights fully hang in view. Her face is large and sharp. Mid 20s.

Subject: A real photograph of a striking adult Korean woman — Korean fresh natural beauty milky ivory-fair complexion with a cool-neutral undertone and real visible pores, mid 20s, glossy dark-brown loose waves past the shoulders, odd-eyed with two clearly different lenses: her left eye has a glowing amber-gold coloured contact lens with a heart-shaped pupil, fully opaque and solidly saturated across the whole iris with no natural brown showing through, the colour bright and unmistakable, with a darker limbal ring, and her right eye has an intense crimson-red coloured contact lens with a greatly enlarged dilated pupil, fully opaque and solidly saturated across the whole iris with no natural brown showing through, the colour bright and unmistakable, with a darker limbal ring, sitting naturally on the irises and clear of the eyelids, the two eye colours both bright and clearly different from each other, eyes opened extremely wide with the whites showing all around the irises, a fixed unblinking stare, brows raised, a wide stretched grin showing teeth, a manic, unhinged expression — a photograph of a real Korean woman's face, not an illustration, not a render. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living skin with visible pores and faint peach-fuzz hairs, slightly asymmetrical with a few small natural beauty marks and freckles, never airbrushed and never smooth like plastic, real wet catchlights in the eyes, individual hair strands catching the light. Her face has been surgically sculpted far beyond her natural look, and these changes override her natural features: her eyes are the star of her face (the shape, size and lenses described here override the eyes of her makeup, while the colours of her eyeshadow and liner follow her makeup): enormous, perfectly round, wide, innocent doe eyes of impossible size, each eye about twice as large as a normal eye with an enormous visible iris that fills almost the whole opening, with a soft white inner liner along the lower lash line, extremely long, thick, curled lashes like little fans and a small softly shaded flick under the lower lashes, in coloured contact lenses, both eyes the same, with a round natural pupil and bright catchlights, still sweet and beautiful; her nose: a high, straight, refined, surgically sculpted nose: a tall, slim, straight bridge, a narrow, pointed, projecting tip and clearly narrow nostril wings with slim, neat nostrils; her jawline and chin: a heart-shaped face: a wide forehead and high, full cheekbones narrowing in a smooth curve into a delicate, pointed, softly rounded chin like the tip of a heart. Every feature is exaggerated but beautiful, balanced and refined, in harmony with the rest of her face, never distorted, never grotesque.

Piercings: A face fully covered with real piercings, about one hundred and fifty-nine in total (not counting the hanging weights), spread over every area so that no area is empty: three separate septum rings of different sizes and shapes through the thin soft wall between the nostrils, in a short stack that ends above the upper lip; four small rings wrapping snugly around each nostril wing; ten small hoop or studs along the edge of the upper lip; sixteen small hoop or studs across the lower lip's edge; ten small ring or studs on the chin; on each ear, two separate large healed openings in the earlobe, one below the other with a clear gap of bare skin between them, each opening holding its own very thick, heavy black cast-iron ring as thick as a finger, a plain solid ring with no open tunnel, and above them sit twenty-nine pieces above the lobe: fourteen classic round O-rings and studs along the helix rim, nine studs and small bars across the upper cartilage and six in the conch and tragus; twenty small studs across the lower half of the forehead just above the brows in even rows, leaving the upper forehead free; sixteen small studs along each cheekbone, well clear of the eyes. The pieces on her face are punk in style: instead of plain studs and rings, the small pieces are safety-pin shaped bars, sharp cone-spike studs and chunky chain-link rings. The left and right sides are balanced. The piercings are packed so densely that the rows touch and overlap, leaving only hairline gaps of bare skin between them, until the face reads as a single armour of metal; the eyes and eyelids stay clear. Stickers: five tiny glow-in-the-dark heart and star stickers are scattered flat on the skin of the lower cheeks and the jawline below the cheekbone studs, clear of the piercings, the eyes and the lips. All the ear weights hang from the bottoms of these two iron rings, and they are not counted in the piercing total: on each ear there are exactly nine separate massive weights, each of a different shape and a different metal, all of them rough, hammered, matte and unpolished, each hanging on its own thick heavy chain of the same metal as the weight: on the left ear dull blue-grey lead a miniature anvil on a shortest chain, dull dark brass a cube-shaped block on a shortest chain, blackened cast iron a teardrop-shaped sinker on a short chain, oxidized dark copper a ship's anchor on a medium chain, rough-cast matte yellow gold a barrel-shaped weight on a medium chain, tarnished dark silver a chunky hexagonal nut-shaped weight with a round hole through the centre on a long chain, dull pewter-grey tin a square-sided cowbell on a longer chain, dark patinated bronze a round bell on a longer chain, rough-cast matte yellow gold a bell-shaped weight like a small temple bell with a flared rim on a longest chain; on the right ear dark patinated bronze a ship's anchor on a shortest chain, oxidized dark copper a chunky hexagonal nut-shaped weight with a round hole through the centre on a shortest chain, rough-cast matte yellow gold a cube-shaped block on a short chain, tarnished dark silver a pyramid-shaped lump on a medium chain, dull blue-grey lead a square-sided cowbell on a medium chain, blackened cast iron a bell-shaped weight like a small temple bell with a flared rim on a long chain, dull dark brass a miniature anvil on a longer chain, dull pewter-grey tin a barrel-shaped weight on a longer chain, dull blue-grey lead a teardrop-shaped sinker on a longest chain. On each ear the two iron rings each carry their own column of weights, the two columns holding 5 and 4 weights, hanging side by side on chains of different lengths and staggered at different heights so every weight is fully visible and none hides another. Every single weight is a massive, dense, solid lump of metal at least as big as her whole fist and clearly larger than her earlobe, rough and matte and unpolished with no shine and no delicate or thin parts; its size does NOT shrink just because there are many of them: the last weight is exactly as big, as thick and as heavy-looking as the first. Each weight alone looks like it weighs several kilograms, each chain is pulled bar-straight and taut, and at a glance every single one looks crushingly, unmistakably heavy, the chains hanging freely in the air, clear of her neck and shoulders, with even the longest chain and its weight ending no lower than the level of her collarbones, never below them and never resting on her chest or body. Because the load is shared between two openings, the weight gently pulls each earlobe down a little into a slightly elongated, soft, healthy loop of skin, only a small natural droop that is just enough to show how heavy the weights are; the lobe never stretches long, never tears or collapses and never hangs down to her neck or shoulder, her head stays upright, and the skin stays smooth and intact, fully healed, with no tearing, no wound, no blood and no redness. The face and ear jewelry is real blackened steel and chrome silver, spiked and studded, with no gemstones, while the hanging weights are always rough, matte, unpolished heavy metal in mixed materials (lead, tin, gold, silver, bronze, copper, brass and iron), sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it.

Hair: her hair is swept back behind both ears, leaving both ears, her jawline and her neck fully visible so every hanging piece is in clear view.

Lighting: The background is a city street at night in the rain, blurred neon signs and car lights in teal and deep blue, out of focus with a shallow depth of field, with no objects and no people in the background, and the background is darker and softer than her face so that her face and the metal are the brightest, sharpest part of the image. The background colours are cool, mid-to-dark tones clearly different from her skin tone, never beige, peach, orange or brown, and never bright. A soft frontal light on her face and ears, so the glints on every piece of metal read clearly against her skin; a thin cool rim light along the hair and shoulders. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
